audit_scope.description: Trust model analysis for Cancun state management (transaction snapshots, account lifecycle, storage operations, transient storage, balance transfers), EIP-6122 (ForkID calculation and peer validation), EIP-712 (typed data signing), EIP-2387 (Muir Glacier fork activation), and EIP-7691 (blob gas parameter increase). Covers state management internals, P2P peer filtering, off-chain signature security, and blob gas economics.

in_scope: State management: transaction snapshots, rollback, account lifecycle
Storage operations: get_storage, set_storage, transient storage
EIP-712 typed data hashing and signing interface
out_of_scope: Internal EVM execution engine (treated as internal component)
Wallet UI/UX for EIP-712 signature approval
Consensus layer Electra blob parameter changes

misclassified_entities.reason: EVM Executor is an internal component of the Execution Layer. It triggers transaction begin/commit/rollback operations as part of the EVM execution engine, not as an external entity.
Smart Contract executing SELFDESTRUCT is internal to the EVM execution context. Contracts are code running within the EL, not external entities.
EVM Storage Opcodes (SLOAD/SSTORE) are internal EVM instructions. They are part of the EL execution engine, not external entities.
EVM Transient Opcodes (TLOAD/TSTORE) are internal EVM instructions for ephemeral storage. They operate within the EL execution context.
Transaction Value Transfer is an internal EVM operation (part of CALL or transaction execution). Value transfers are initiated by the EVM, not by an external entity.
Chain Configuration is an internal data source loaded from the node's local configuration files. It is not an external entity but part of the node's initialization data.
Wallet User in EIP-712 context represents the human approving/rejecting signing requests via wallet UI. This is a UI trust boundary, not a network-level external entity to the EL.
Malicious Actor in EIP-712 context is a threat actor attempting signature replay attacks. Attackers are not external entities but threat scenarios against the signing and verification interfaces.
Verifying Smart Contract is an on-chain contract that verifies EIP-712 signatures. It runs within the EVM and is internal to the EL, not an external entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P DevP2P protocol (ForkID exchange during handshake, block propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are untrusted network participants. They exchange ForkIDs during connection handshake for compatibility filtering (EIP-6122). Peers with incompatible or stale ForkIDs are rejected. Peers also propagate blocks for Muir Glacier fork validation (EIP-2387). All data from peers is independently validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Decentralized Application
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Dapps requesting EIP-712 typed data signatures are untrusted. They may attempt to encode misleading structures where displayed meaning differs from verified meaning. The wallet must faithfully display typed data to users. Domain separators provide cross-domain replay protection but same-domain replay protection is left to application implementers.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block proposal via consensus layer (Engine API)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers (validators/proposers) create blocks with blob transactions. They interact with the EL via the Engine API which is authenticated with JWT. They are semi-trusted because they are authenticated and economically staked, but their blocks must still be fully validated against blob count limits (max 9 blobs per EIP-7691) and gas constraints.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Peer ForkIDs are validated against local chain configuration. Incompatible peers (ErrRemoteStale, ErrLocalIncompatibleOrStale) are rejected. CRC32 checksums provide fork identification but not cryptographic security. Peers may lie about their ForkID but will be detected upon block exchange.

Dapp-provided typed data is parsed and displayed to the user for approval. The domain separator (name, version, chainId, verifyingContract) provides cross-domain and cross-chain replay protection. Same-domain replay protection must be implemented at the application level via nonces. The wallet must not sign without user approval.

Block producers are authenticated via JWT on the Engine API. Blocks are validated for blob count (max 9), blob gas usage (max 1,179,648), and all standard consensus rules. Even authenticated block proposals are fully validated before acceptance.

coverage_gaps: Nine entities were misclassified: EXT-EVM, EXT-CONTRACT, EXT-EVM-STORAGE, EXT-EVM-TRANSIENT, EXT-TX-VALUE (all internal EVM components), EXT-CHAIN-CONFIG (internal data), EXT-USER (UI boundary), EXT-ATTACKER (threat actor), EXT-VERIFYING-CONTRACT (internal EVM contract). These represent internal EVM execution mechanics and threat scenarios, not external network entities.
